title: Squiggle positions are regex-scraped from human-readable error strings instead of structured parser output
existing_state: ScriptParser.Validate returns List<string> (ScriptParser.cs:4181-4185) — positions known at validation time are flattened into prose. ScriptEditorValidationService then reverse-engineers locations from the message text with three regexes (ScriptEditorValidationService.cs:9-16): any message lacking a parseable 'Line N' lands on line 1 with a full-line squiggle (line 164), and the underlined token is found by the FIRST case-insensitive IndexOf occurrence in that line (line 172), which underlines the wrong instance when the token appears twice. MapExceptionToDiagnostic does the same scrape on exception text (193-205). This structure means every new validation message added to the 4000+-line Validate method must remember the exact 'Line N:' string format or the editor silently mis-places the squiggle — the contract is an undocumented string convention between two services, and there is no test that can catch a formatting miss generically.
recommendation: Add a structured diagnostic type to the parser (line, column/token span, severity, message) and a Validate overload that returns it, populating positions at the emit sites that already compute them (the originalYaml/lines plumbing at ScriptParser.cs:4188 shows line info is already threaded through). Migrate incrementally: structured where available, fall back to the existing string-scrape for unconverted sites, then have ScriptEditorValidationService consume the structured list directly and keep string formatting only for the MessageBox/manual-validate path. The regex scrapers become dead code at the end.
user_benefit: Squiggles land on the actual offending line/token instead of defaulting to line 1 or underlining the wrong duplicate — and new validation rules can't silently break editor placement via a string-format mismatch.
